newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Senate votes to approve extradition.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Senate votes to approve extradition.

text.p: Colombia's Senate gave its preliminary but overwhelming support on Tuesday to legislation that would lift the country's constitutional ban on the extradition of drug lords and other criminals wanted for trial abroad.
The Senate, many of whose 102 members failed to show up for a heated debate over the bill that would lift the ban introduced in 1991, approved it by a vote of 62 to 15.

The bill must still be approved in further debates in the Senate and House -- and final passage was unlikely to come before the first half of next year -- but the preliminary vote signalled surprisingly strong support for the practice that polls show most Colombians still oppose.

In a recent survey published in Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper, the country's leading daily, nearly 70 percent of Colombians said they thought a revival of extradition would prompt another wave of "narcoterrorism" like the one Colombia suffered under in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Hundreds of people, including three presidential candidates, an attorney general and countless judges, journalists and police, were killed in a campaign of bombings, assassinations and kidnappings that traffickers unleashed to press for the current ban on extradition.

Tuesday's vote came against the backdrop of a wave of reported threats against supporters of extradition, including senior lawmakers. It also came after last week's discovery of a huge car bomb in the southwest city of Cali that police said was planted by drug barons opposed to extradition.

The car bomb was discovered outside a chemical plant owned by the husband of Sen. Claudia Blum, a leading proponent of extradition who cited death threats as her reason for requesting a leave of absence from her Senate duties early on Tuesday.
